title: Scene-Text Oriented Referring Expression Comprehension
research_question: Can referring-expression comprehension be improved for expressions that depend on text visible in an image by explicitly aligning referring expressions, scene-text semantics, and localized visual regions?
methodology: The paper introduces scene-text oriented referring expression comprehension, extending conventional REC to cases where scene text helps identify or disambiguate a target object. It proposes the Scene Text Awareness Network, which grounds expression-correlated scene text through a Correlated Text Extraction module and activates relevant local image regions through a Correlated Region Activation module. The authors introduce the RefText benchmark and evaluate the proposed approach on this task. The accessible publisher source exposed only the abstract, so detailed training settings, ablations, and numerical result tables could not be independently inspected there.

key_findings.finding: The paper identifies scene text as an informative cue for object identification and disambiguation that conventional referring-expression comprehension methods largely neglect.
The proposed ST-REC task explicitly incorporates text appearing in the scene into referring-expression grounding.
STAN combines Correlated Text Extraction and Correlated Region Activation to connect expression-relevant scene text with localized visual regions.
The authors introduce RefText as a benchmark for scene-text-oriented referring-expression comprehension.
The official project repository describes RefText as containing approximately 31,000 manually generated referring expressions for 11,000 objects over 4,594 images.
key_findings.section: Official STAN repository accompanying the paper

key_findings.finding: The abstract reports that STAN performs effectively on the proposed task, but the accessible publisher abstract does not provide the detailed numerical comparisons needed to quantify the improvement.

limitations: The accessible publisher page exposed only the abstract, so the paper's author-stated limitations, detailed ablations, and numerical comparisons could not be verified from the paper text.
The method depends on detecting or recognizing scene text before or during grounding, making upstream text-recognition quality a likely dependency; the abstract does not quantify this sensitivity.
raw_claims: Conventional referring-expression comprehension largely focuses on ordinary visual attributes and gives little attention to scene text.
Text visible inside an image can help distinguish otherwise ambiguous objects.
The paper formulates a scene-text-oriented variant of referring-expression comprehension.
STAN explicitly links referring expressions with semantically relevant scene text.
Correlated Text Extraction is designed to obtain scene-text information related to the referring expression.
Correlated Region Activation is designed to emphasize local visual regions associated with relevant scene text.
RefText is introduced as the evaluation benchmark for the task.
The accompanying official repository provides implementation resources and RefText data.
The accessible abstract states that the proposed method performs effectively but does not expose its detailed numerical results.
